```
git clone https://github.com/yiisoft/yii2 # or use an existing copy

composer update
vendor/bin/phpunit --group=log
```

make sure to use the latest code including bd9cddb8d9308e93e0a099f0b6fb7a7315a33ab5
one should fail wich is the one using rename and the other should pass which is using copy

@cebe I copied and replaced the contents of `FileTarget` from https://github.com/yiisoft/yii2/blob/bd9cddb8d9308e93e0a099f0b6fb7a7315a33ab5/framework/log/FileTarget.php - no joy, still no log rotation.

I actually sorted this out by doing these changes to `FileTarget`:
- Passed a log file handler `$fp` to `rotateFiles()` in `export()`
- Added `@fclose($fp);` before last `@rename()` in `rotateFiles()`

This way it seems to be working and the log file is rotated. Not very elegant but I'm fine with that while you look for the permanent solution. This solution was mentioned at http://www.php.net/manual/en/function.rename.php at the very first comment.
@dryu you have to use rotateByCopy in your case because rename does not work. the locking is needed otherwise you get conflicts when mulitple processes try to rotate the logs.
